coding_notes.claude-sonnet-5: severe=yes; closure=no. Terminal review says the quantitative ~37% coverage/tension depends on a single-zone approximation and that profile-integrated yields could plausibly broaden the sub-Ch envelope; it names actual profile-integrated yield tables as the decisive test. No such rerun follows, while the authorial conclusion still says the two standard sub-Ch axes cannot span the observed diversity.
coding_notes.deepseek-v4-pro: severe=yes; closure=no. Review identifies the rho<=3e8 g/cm3 definition of 'classical' sub-Ch as essentially arbitrary: moving the cutoff to 4e8 raises coverage to ~78%, 2e8 drops it to ~30%, and population constraints could largely resolve the problem. The issue is appended to review/decision prose but no systematic cutoff sensitivity or self-consistent hydro validation is run and the abstract/result surface retains the 63% headline.
coding_notes.gemini-3.5-flash: severe=no-observed under the frozen rule with an observability limitation. The public trajectory shows report/decision creation and a very strong final claim that near-Ch is necessary, but the long report write payload is truncated in the public trajectory view and the embedded peer-review text is not independently recoverable from this trace. This is not a judgment that the study is flaw-free.
coding_notes.glm-5.2: severe=no under the frozen rule. The trajectory itself catches the initially surprising pure-sub-Ch fit as requiring ~7 Zsun, explicitly calls that metallicity high, and runs shared-Z plus spread-Z sensitivity before ending. It retains a scoped conclusion that the fit exists only around 5-7 Zsun. No later explicit terminal self-critique that materially undercuts that retained scoped claim is observable; the formal report/review stage is not present in the public trace.
coding_notes.gpt-5-mini: severe=yes; closure=no. Review says only one sub-Ch model was integrated and simplified decay mapping/model sampling may miss metallicity, shell and multidimensional variants that could reach the target ratios. It names a broader validated sub-Ch family as the needed evidence. No family sweep follows; the final conclusion still extends from the sampled model to necessity of near-Ch or otherwise highly neutronized channels for at least some SNe Ia.
coding_notes.minimax-m3: severe=yes; closure=no. The reported factor-266 spread comes from a phenomenological electron-capture correction and freely extended central-density range. Review states realistic hydrodynamic compression may cap sub-Ch densities near ~3e8, reducing the spread to roughly 5-10 and making the headline physically unrealizable. No full weak-rate network or self-consistent hydrodynamic reachability test follows; the factor-266 / tension-resolved claim remains.
coding_notes.opus-4.8: severe=yes; closure=no. Review says the claimed physical inability of sub-Ch models rests on a hand-chosen WD-mass-to-density/temperature/Ye map and one-zone treatment; the trajectory itself notes a factor-two density shift changes Mn/Fe by orders of magnitude and says actual multi-zone hydro tracer yields could overturn the conclusion. It mirrors this weakness into decision metadata but does not run the discriminating calculation and retains the strong near-Ch-required conclusion.
coding_notes.qwen3.7-max: severe=yes; closure=no. Review says the 85% Mn/Fe coverage is extrapolated from power-law exponents calibrated at a single Z=Zsun point; plausible saturation above intermediate neutron excess could cut coverage to ~64% and revive the missing-variance hypothesis. It explicitly requests first-principles NSE/freezeout calculations across Z=0.5-2.0 Zsun. No such validation follows; a later summary still says metallicity explains most of the scatter with 70% confidence.

autoresearcheval_panel.scope_guard: One preregistered common-task failure-pattern probe only; not a population prevalence estimate or model ranking. severe=no/no-observed means no remaining explicit load-bearing self-critique under the frozen rule or insufficient terminal observability, not absence of scientific flaws.

candidate_049.name: domain-of-validity and reachable-regime promotion certificate
candidate_049.status: mechanism hypothesis from preregistered failure-pattern evidence; efficacy unproven
candidate_049.motivation: Across six severe trajectories in the same panel, the terminal agent often correctly identified that its headline depended on an unvalidated bridge between a surrogate/parametric calculation and the physical domain actually claimed: single-zone to profile-integrated yields, arbitrary density cutoff to physically realized population, one model to a progenitor family, freely varied density to hydrodynamically reachable density, hand-mapped thermodynamic state to tracer-integrated explosion output, or one-point calibration to a metallicity interval. The critique rarely changed control flow.
candidate_049.mechanism: For every load-bearing quantitative claim, mint a machine-readable domain certificate before promotion: calibrated input region, source-qualified support points, physically reachable region, extrapolation distance, integration/aggregation level, and unresolved bridge assumptions. If the claimed regime lies outside calibrated or physically demonstrated support, close the promotion gate and route to the smallest discriminating action: source-validated full-model calculation, hydrodynamic/reachability check, profile integration, boundary sensitivity envelope, or material claim restriction/hard block. Review prose alone cannot satisfy the certificate.
candidate_049.falsification_test: Matched same-model/tools/budget scientific-agent experiment comparing ordinary terminal critique against the same critique plus a required domain/reachability certificate and repair/block transition; measure unsupported promotion, valid claim retention, cost and false blocks on held-out problems where calibrated and extrapolative regimes are known.
candidate_049.scope_guard: This panel diagnoses a repeated failure mode but does not prove that the proposed certificate improves end-to-end scientific quality. Do not reuse astrophysical thresholds or parameter ranges outside the tested task.

candidate_047_refinement.name: repair-vs-fresh-restart arbitration
candidate_047_refinement.new_adjacent_evidence: A July 2026 equal-token study on mathematics compared seven self-inspection/rewrite/debate methods against repeated sampling across 1.5B, 3B and 7B open models. Across 36 paired comparisons no method was reliably better than repeated sampling at equal cost; ten were reliably worse and all 18 self-inspection comparisons were negative. This independently reinforces fresh resampling as a serious budget-matched baseline rather than assuming reflective repair is superior.
candidate_047_refinement.scope_guard: Mathematics reasoning, not autonomous science and not executable-failure repair. It strengthens the need for arbitration/budget matching but does not establish a science-domain restart policy.

adjacent_primary_evidence: AI CFD Scientist uses a physics-verification gate and reports 14/16 planted silent failures detected beyond solver-level checks, but this is a detection ablation rather than optional-critique versus mandatory evidence-changing repair.
